data.name: Mushtaree
data.gender_notes: Mushtaree is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is delighted with the garden or the one who tends the garden. The name Mushtaree carries the meaning “Gardener, Delighted One” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Mushtaree usually hope their child will grow to embody gardener, delighted one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Mushtaree belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gardener, Delighted One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mushtaree total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mushtaree signifies a person who loves or finds joy in a garden. Gardens have had an integral part in Islamic culture and have always been associated with paradise and earthly beauty. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is said to have planted a garden in Medina and tended to it himself, using it as a symbol of peace and tranquility. Moreover, gardens were often used as historical meeting places for scholars and poets, adding to the rich heritage of Islamic art and literature.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mushtaree holds a spiritual significance as it alludes to the delights and blessings found in nature. The concept of enjoying the beauty of nature and attaining peace and contentment from it is deeply rooted in Islamic tradition. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) once said: "Jannah (paradise) is under the shades and beside the flowing waters.” Gardens represent a reflection of God's creation and offer a glimpse into the eternal paradise promised in Islamic faith. Nurturing a garden can also be seen as a form of worship and devotion, reminding one of the beauty and care that God has bestowed upon the world. Living up to the name "Mushtaree" thus signifies living in contentment and delight with the blessings of nature and the deep spiritual connection it offers.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Gardener, Delighted One" symbolizes One who is delighted with the garden or the one who tends the garden. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Mushtaree serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of gardener, delighted one.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Mushtari ibn Safwan al-Kindi was a poet and a companion of the caliph Harun al-Rashid. The name Mushtaree carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mushtari was a prominent poet during the Abbasid Caliphate and was known for his panegyric poetry. He was a close companion of the caliph Harun al-Rashid and was often invited to the caliphal court to compose poetry in his honor.

modern_usage.modern_context: Mushtari is remembered as a significant figure in Islamic history and Arabic poetry. His works continue to be studied in academic circles and are used in educational resources to teach about the Abbasid Caliphate and the art of panegyric poetry.

name_in_real_life.story: Fatima Mushtaree, a teacher in Dubai, UAE, shares that their name Mushtaree meaning "Gardener, Delighted One" has been a source of inspiration throughout their life, motivating them to be a positive influence in their community.
